channels.title: Kilowatt Nation
channels.description:
How America got electricity — and who paid for it.

Kilowatt Nation tells the story of the American power grid through the people who built it, the money and deals that shaped it, and the nights it failed. Rural electrification and the farm cooperatives that strung their own lines. The utility empires, the men who ran them, and the bargains that decided who owns the wire outside your house. The great blackouts — 1965, New York in 1977, the Northeast in 2003, Texas in 2021 — reconstructed minute by minute from official reports, archival photographs and the accounts of those on shift.

Every episode is a long-form documentary on American electrical infrastructure and industrial history: power plants, dams, transmission lines, substations and the companies behind them, from the first city systems of the 1880s to the grid we depend on now. Sourced from public archives and government investigations, told for anyone who has worked in this industry — or lost power because of it.

channels.title: Forgotten Blue Collar America
channels.description:
This is the America that built the country with its hands. Steel mills, rail yards, auto plants, coal mines, shipyards. Men who punched a clock at 6 a.m., carried a lunch pail, and came home with grease under their fingernails and pride in their work.

That world is gone now. The factories are silent. The whistles don't blow anymore. The foremen, the unwritten rules, the lunch pail customs, the brotherhood of the shop floor. Most of it vanished within a single generation, and nobody wrote it down.

We bring it back. Every video uncovers the forgotten rules, lost rituals, and vanished traditions of blue-collar American workplaces from the 1920s through the 1970s.

Subscribe and help us keep the memory of blue collar America alive before the last man who lived it is gone

channels.title: Steel & Sweat
channels.description:
America wasn't built in boardrooms. It was built in the dark, inside furnaces, under 40-ton machines, by men who knew the odds weren't in their favor.
Steel & Sweat tells the stories of the machines, the industries, and the workers that forged the United States into the most powerful industrial nation on Earth — and the brutal price paid to get there.
From the smoking blast furnaces of Pittsburgh to the death-trap logging camps of Michigan. Every video is a deep dive into a forgotten corner of American industrial history — told with the detail, drama, and respect these stories deserve.

channels.title: Amos Miller
channels.description:
Hello, I’m Amos Miller, a 67-year-old Amish farmer living in rural Pennsylvania.

People outside our community often consider my family “backward” because we use very little technology. I don’t want them to keep misunderstanding us or assuming that we live this way because we are poor or don’t know how to use modern technology.

Through this channel, I will spend the rest of my life showing that we choose not to depend on these technologies—not because we don’t understand how to use them. And perhaps, by watching my videos and applying these methods to your everyday life, you may save quite a bit of money along the way.

Topics include food storage and preservation, frugal cooking, pantry systems, gardening, cleaning, home maintenance, seasonal living, and practical household skills.
